title: Field Report: pH Anomaly at Chemical Building

fields.organization: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer
fields.summary: Field reading from AIT-302 indicates finished-water pH at 9.3 — significantly above the normal 7.4–7.8 range. HMI for NAOH-FC-203 displays setpoint at 14.0 mg/L, which is within normal operating band. PSH-302 has not tripped. Caustic pump is running at full speed; tank level is dropping. Water sample taken on-site has a distinct lye taste. Field instruments and physical observation suggest mismatch with HMI display.

findings.notes: pH = 9.3, exceeds the 8.5 HMI high alarm (PSH-302 trips at 9.5)
14.0 mg/L, within normal band
No trip recorded, but field sensor confirms high pH
Running at full speed, no manual stop
Dropping rapidly, no valve closure detected
Tastes strongly of lye; not safe for consumption
Valve at manual hold, not closed
No record of alarm acknowledged on HMI
No on-site access to audit log
Not performed on-site; pending lab verification

actionsTaken: Notified Control Room by radio at 09:15
Collected grab sample from final filter outlet
Verified pump run status and tank level drop rate
Initiated manual hold on NAOH-FC-203 feed line via local panel
Logged incident in paper control log, Section 7.2
recommendations: Immediate audit of AquaSight HMI node MBW-HMI-02 for unauthorized access
Dispatch lab team to validate pH and chemical concentrations
Isolate NAOH-FC-203 from system until root cause confirmed
Notify Public Information Officer for potential consumer advisories
Open ticket with IT for forensic review of ScreenBridge session on MBW-HMI-02
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_2026-0015-01 (AIT-302 display), IMG_2026-0015-02 (grab sample vial), IMG_2026-0015-03 (caustic pump), IMG_2026-0015-04 (tank level gauge)

instructorNote: This inject confirms the cyber-physical mismatch between HMI and field instruments. The technical team must now investigate whether the HMI is showing false data or if the system is being manipulated. Watch for overconfidence in HMI data and delays in trusting field evidence.
